Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a massive regression this morning starting ~09:25 UTC: p95 and p99 latencies for our hosted embeddings route jumped by ~10–18s and error rate spiked to 7% for ~15 minutes. Attached a screenshot of the latency graph and a sample log from one of our workers. This is impacting user-facing indexing jobs and causing customer alerts.

Key facts:
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/embeddings (model: redwood-emb-large)
- Spike window: 09:25–09:40 UTC
- Errors: 5xx timeout errors + request queueing observed

This is P1 for us. Please escalate.

Thanks,

Naomi / team, quick triage notes:

- What I see in logs (attached sample-llm-logs-20280315.txt): when autoscaler fired we moved traffic to a newly resumed GPU pool. Pool 'resume' handshake (VM boot + driver init + runtime warm) has an outlier tail of ~12–18s in the current build. While that happens requests are queued at the routing layer which amplifies p95/p99.
- Error spikes are a mix of upstream timeouts and transient 5xx from the runtime when kernel init fails under contention.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (short-term, can be executed in the next 30–60 minutes):
1) Enable warm-pool hold for FinPulse (pre-allocate 4 warm instances to reduce resume path) — requires quota bump; I can spin up a temporary pool if allowed.
2) Reroute FinPulse traffic to Dedicated reserved pool (if customer has it) or direct less latency-sensitive traffic to hosted degraded model.
3) Reduce per-request max_batch_size for the embeddings route for the next 2 hours to reduce queueing backlog.

Longer-term (engineering):
- Fix handshake path to parallelize driver+runtime init to knock down resume tail.
- Add proactive warm-pool suggestions to Redwood Optimize based on usage patterns.

Attachments: sample-llm-logs-20280315.txt

I'll start with (1) if ops approves quota. Can someone from infra (Vivek or Aditya) approve emergency warm capacity?

—Dylan
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
